title: Cognitive and Autonomic Load Monitoring in Operations
summary:
Physicians are frequently exposed to high levels of occupational stress, with surgeons experiencing particularly intense stress during operative procedures.

The aim of this project is to establish wearable devices capable of reliably assessing stress using heart rate variability (HRV) and electrodermal activity (EDA).

Building on this, the effectiveness of brief relaxation exercises on subjective stress levels and error rates will be investigated in the setting of a robotic surgery simulation.

In a subsequent step, the overarching objective is to enable real-time stress detection in the operating room, allowing continuous monitoring of both the surgeon’s stress level and the quality of the procedure, with the possibility of targeted stress reduction when necessary.

In the long term, this approach aims to promote surgeons’ health while simultaneously improving surgical quality.

interventions.name:
Intervention group:
The intervention group performs a breathing exercise with prolonged exhalation for 3 minutes before performing the training exercises on the DaVinci simulator.

Control group:
The control group lets their thoughts run free for 3 minutes before performing the training exercises on the DaVinci simulator.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria are physicians or students, age 18 years or older, provision of written informed consent, and sufficient German language proficiency to ensure full understanding of the study information and instructions.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are age under 18 years and insufficient German language proficiency to ensure full understanding of the study information and instructions.
